intro: High above the Aegean, in Çanakkale province, lies Assos, an ancient city whose story begins in the 7th century BC. Here a temple of Athena crowns the city where Aristotle taught.
history: Aristotle lived and taught here for three years. The city itself was known for its andesite walls and its busy harbour.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Temple of Athena and the ancient harbour, then follow the city walls to the necropolis, and end at the agora.
facts: Did you know? Assos sarcophagi were believed to consume flesh — hence the word 'sarcophagus'. Aristotle spent three years here, founded a school, and married the ruler's niece, and he began his biological work in the gulf below. The Temple of Athena is the only archaic Doric temple in Anatolia. And Saint Paul walked here from Troas on his third journey and took ship from this harbour; Acts records it by name.
outro: This brings our journey through Assos to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Philosophers and travellers have passed this way before you; let these stones wait for those who come next. Enjoy your visit.
